items.title: Poacher Turned Gamekeeper: HHS’ Matt Zorn on Ibogaine, Right to Try and the Psychedelics Executive Order

summaries.en:
The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services is taking psychedelics seriously—and now we're hearing directly from the people making it happen. Matt Zorn, Deputy General Counsel at HHS, just gave his first major interview since stepping into a role that's reshaping how the government approaches these medicines. He's diving into the details of ibogaine access, Right to Try pathways, and what the Psychedelics Executive Order actually means for patients and researchers. This is what real movement looks like: not just policy on paper, but people inside the system genuinely engaging with how psychedelics could transform healthcare.

Zorn's conversation—held at The Psychedelic Healthcare Forum in New York—signals that psychedelic research isn't stuck in the margins anymore. It's moving into the halls where decisions get made. As more clinical evidence piles up showing promise for depression, addiction, and trauma, the regulatory landscape is finally catching up. These insider discussions matter because they show us how science gets translated into actual access for people who need it.
summaries.da:
USA's sundhedsministerium tager psykedelika seriøst—og nu hører vi direkte fra mennesker, der laver det muligt. Matt Zorn, Deputy General Counsel på HHS, gav lige hans første store interview siden han startede i en rolle, der omdanner, hvordan regeringen tilgår disse mediciner. Han dykker ned i detaljerne omkring ibogain-adgang, Right to Try-veje og hvad den psykedelika-præsidentialordre faktisk betyder for patienter og forskere. Det er sådan virkeligt fremskridt ser ud: ikke bare politik på papir, men mennesker inde i systemet, der seriøst engagerer sig i, hvordan psykedelika kunne transformere sundhedsvæsenet.

Zorns samtale—afholdt på The Psychedelic Healthcare Forum i New York—signalerer, at psykedelika-forskning ikke længere er hængende på margenen. Det rykker ind i de rum, hvor beslutninger træffes. Efterhånden som mere klinisk evidens viser løfte for depression, afhængighed og trauma, følger det regulatoriske landskab endelig med. Disse interne diskussioner betyder noget, fordi de viser os, hvordan videnskab bliver oversat til reel adgang for mennesker, der har brug for det.

items.title: Treatment expectation is associated with willingness to participate in a psychedelic clinical trial

summaries.en: Who signs up for psychedelic trials? A new study reveals that your expectations matter more than you might think. Researchers surveyed nearly 1,000 chronic pain patients and found that people with positive expectations about outcomes were significantly more likely to join a psychedelic clinical trial, while those worried about negative effects were much less interested. Interestingly, negative expectations proved to be the single strongest predictor—stronger even than personality traits. The study used surveys to measure personality, psychological flexibility, and outcome expectations in chronic pain patients. This finding matters because it hints at a potential bias in how psychedelic trials are recruiting participants: we might be enrolling people who are naturally more optimistic and risk-tolerant, which could skew results. As psychedelic research expands toward mainstream medicine, understanding who participates—and why—becomes crucial for making sure the science is solid and findings actually apply to real-world patients.
summaries.da: Hvem tilmelder sig psykedelika-studier? Et nyt studie afslører, at dine forventninger betyder mere end du måske tror. Forskerne spurgte næsten 1.000 kronisk smertepatienter og fandt, at mennesker med positive forventninger til resultaterne var væsentligt mere villige til at deltage i et psykedelika-klinisk forsøg, mens de bekymrede væk fra det. Interessant nok viste sig negative forventninger at være den stærkeste enkeltfaktor—endda stærkere end personlighedstræk. Studiet brugte spørgeskemaer til at måle personlighed, psykologisk fleksibilitet og resultatforventninger hos kronisk smertepatienter. Dette fund er vigtigt, fordi det tyder på en mulig skævvridning i, hvordan psykedelika-forsøg rekrutterer deltagere: vi risikerer at tilmelde mennesker, der naturligt er mere optimistiske og risikotolerante, hvilket kunne påvirke resultaterne. Når psykedelika-forskningen ekspanderer mod almindelig medicin, bliver det afgørende at forstå, hvem der deltager—og hvorfor—for at sikre, at videnskaben er solid og fundet gælder for rigtige patienter.

items.title: Intravenous Ketamine for Depressed and Suicidal Adolescents in the Emergency Department: A Randomized Double-Blind Trial.

summaries.en: Young people in crisis are waiting. Emergency rooms overflow with suicidal teens, many stuck for hours without treatment while psychiatric beds fill up. A new study tested whether ketamine—a fast-acting drug showing promise in adults—could offer real relief. A single IV dose reduced depression and suicidal thoughts in adolescents with treatment-resistant depression, with effects visible within hours. This randomized, placebo-controlled trial followed teens aged 12-17 who arrived at the ER expressing suicidal ideation, measuring their symptoms before and after treatment. The results matter because psychedelics and dissociatives like ketamine work differently than traditional antidepressants—they don't just adjust brain chemistry gradually, they seem to create rapid shifts in how people experience their crisis. As research expands into younger populations, we're learning that sometimes the fastest path to safety isn't waiting for the old tools to work.
summaries.da: Unge mennesker i krise venter. Skadestuer løber over med selvmordstruede teenagere, mange sidder fast i timevis uden behandling mens psykiatriske senge fyldes op. Et nyt studie testede, om ketamin—et hurtigt virkende stof, der lover meget hos voksne—kunne give virkelig lindring. En enkelt IV-dosis reducerede depression og selvmordstanker hos unge med behandlingsresistent depression, med effekter synlige inden for timer. Dette randomiserede, placebo-kontrolleret forsøg fulgte teenagere i alderen 12-17, som mødte op på skadestuen med selvmordstanker, og målte deres symptomer før og efter behandling. Resultaterne betyder noget, fordi psykedelika og dissociativa som ketamin virker anderledes end traditionelle antidepressiva—de justerer ikke blot hjernekemi gradvist, de synes at skabe hurtige skift i, hvordan mennesker oplever deres krise. Mens forskningen udvides til yngre populationer, lærer vi, at vejen til sikkerhed nogle gange løber gennem værktøjer, vi endnu ikke fuldt ud forstår.

items.title: Clinical Evidence on Psilocybin and Its Representation in Media Reporting: A Systematic Review.

summaries.en:
Psilocybin is making headlines as a breakthrough for depression, PTSD, and anxiety—but here's the catch: the media is getting ahead of the science. A new systematic review found that while clinical trials of psilocybin have grown steadily since 2018, news coverage has exploded even faster and often plays up the promise while downplaying the caution. Depression dominates both the research and the news cycle, but media outlets are way more interested in PTSD and anxiety than the actual trial data supports. This gap between what the evidence actually shows and what people are reading matters—it shapes expectations and understanding at a critical moment in psychedelics research.

Scientists reviewed 70 published clinical trials and 172 media articles from 2014 onward, comparing what each said about efficacy and safety. The findings reveal something important as psychedelics move toward mainstream medicine: we need smarter conversations between researchers, journalists, and the public. The science is genuinely promising—but it's still early, and the most helpful thing we can do right now is stay honest about what we know, what we're still learning, and why that distinction matters.
summaries.da:
Psykedelika bliver præsenteret i medierne som et gennembrud for depression, PTSD og angst—men her er fangsten: medierne er på forhånd af videnskaben. En ny systematisk gennemgang viste, at selvom kliniske forsøg med psykedelika er vokset støt siden 2018, er nyhedsdækningen eksploderet endnu hurtigere og overdriver ofte løfterne, mens forsigtigheden negligeres. Depression dominerer både forskningen og nyhedscyklussen, men medierne er langt mere interesserede i PTSD og angst end de faktiske forsøgsdata understøtter. Dette gab mellem det, som videnskaben virkelig viser, og hvad mennesker læser, betyder noget—det former forventninger og forståelse på et kritisk tidspunkt i psykedelika-forskningen.

Videnskabsfolk gennemgik 70 publicerede kliniske forsøg og 172 mediartikler fra 2014 og frem, og sammenlignede hvad hver sagde om effekt og sikkerhed. Resultaterne afsløring noget vigtigt, mens psykedelika bevæger sig mod mainstream-medicin: vi har brug for smartere samtaler mellem forskere, journalister og publikum. Videnskaben er virkelig lovende—men det er stadig tidligt, og det mest hjælpsomme vi kan gøre lige nu er at være ærlige om hvad vi ved, hvad vi stadig lærer, og hvorfor den forskel betyder noget.

items.title: Caution before canonisation: a clinical and implementation science perspective on psychedelics.

summaries.en: Psilocybin and MDMA are showing real promise in clinical trials—patients with depression, PTSD, and addiction are experiencing rapid symptom improvements when these psychedelics are given within proper therapeutic settings. But here's the catch: most studies are small, follow people for short periods, and don't always tell us the full safety picture. Researchers gave 100+ studies a hard look through clinical, ethical, and practical lenses, and their conclusion is honest: we have proof these psychedelics *can* work under controlled conditions, but we're nowhere near ready to roll them out widely yet. The field needs stronger, longer-term evidence and better real-world testing before psychedelic therapies move from promise to standard practice—and that rigorous work is exactly what's happening right now.
summaries.da: Psilocybin og MDMA viser rigtig potentiale i kliniske forsøg—patienter med depression, PTSD og afhængighed oplever hurtig forbedring når psykedelika gives inden for ordnede terapirammer. Men der er en hage: de fleste studier er små, følger mennesker kort tid, og fortæller ikke altid hele sikkerhedsbilledet. Forskere gennemgik 100+ studier fra flere vinkler—klinik, etik, praktisk gennemførelse—og deres konklusion er ærlig: vi har bevis på at psykedelika *kan* virke under kontrollerede forhold, men vi er langt fra parate til at rulle dem ud bredt endnu. Området har brug for stærkere, længerevarende beviser og bedre test i virkelighedens verden før psykedelika-terapi går fra løfte til standard praksis—og det grundige arbejde er præcis det der sker nu.

items.title: Clinical Evidence on Psilocybin and Its Representation in Media Reporting

summaries.en: Psilocybin is getting a lot of buzz as a potential depression treatment, but a new study reveals a gap between what the science actually shows and what headlines are saying. Researchers found that while clinical trials have grown significantly since 2018, media coverage tends to emphasize benefits while downplaying safety concerns and uncertainties—creating a rosier picture than the evidence supports. The team analyzed 70 published clinical trials and 172 media articles over the past decade, tracking how efficacy and safety claims were reported. This matters because how the public understands psychedelics shapes policy, funding, and people's hopes. The findings highlight why clear, balanced science communication is crucial as psychedelic research accelerates—we need media that honors both the genuine promise and the honest limitations of what we know so far.
summaries.da: Psykedelika får massive medieopmærksomhed som potentiel behandling mod depression, men ny forskning viser et gab mellem hvad videnskaben faktisk viser og hvad overskrifterne siger. Forskerne fandt at selvom kliniske forsøg er vokset markant siden 2018, har mediernes dækning tendens til at fremhæve fordele mens sikkerhed og usikkerhed nedtones—og skaber dermed et mere optimistisk billede end beviserne underbygger. Holdet analyserede 70 publicerede kliniske forsøg og 172 medieartiikler over det seneste årti og sporede hvordan effekt- og sikkerhedspåstande blev rapporteret. Det betyder noget fordi hvordan offentligheden forstår psykedelika påvirker politik, finansiering og menneskers håb. Fundet understreger hvor vigtig præcis, afbalanceret videnskabskommunikation er mens psykedelikaforskningen accelererer—vi skal have medier der respekterer både det reelle potentiale og de ægte begrænsninger af hvad vi ved indtil nu.

items.title: Spatiotemporal remodeling in habenula marks the onset of depression-related phenotypes

summaries.en: Scientists have pinpointed the exact moment depression starts to take hold in the brain—and it's surprisingly specific. Using advanced imaging in mice exposed to chronic stress, researchers watched neurons in a tiny brain region called the lateral habenula begin firing excessively in response to negative events, triggering a cascade of molecular changes that led to depression-like behavior. The striking part? This whole process was reversed by ketamine, an antidepressant showing real promise in clinical trials. The study mapped out the precise timeline and geography of these changes using cutting-edge spatial transcriptomics, essentially creating a molecular map of where and when stress rewires the brain. This work fits perfectly into a growing picture: psychedelics and related compounds like ketamine don't just mask symptoms—they seem to interrupt the actual biological machinery driving depression right at its inception, opening doors to catching and treating the condition much earlier than we can now.
summaries.da: Forskere har præcist identificeret det øjeblik, hvor depression begynder at tage fat i hjernen—og det er overraskende specifikt. Ved hjælp af avanceret billedbehandling hos mus udsat for kronisk stress observerede de neuroner i en minuscul hjernedel kaldet lateral habenula begynde at fyre overdrevent som reaktion på negative begivenheder, hvilket udløste en kaskade af molekylære ændringer, der førte til depressionsagtig adfærd. Det slående? Hele denne proces blev vendt ved ketamin, et antidepressivum, som viser real lovende resultater i kliniske forsøg. Studiet kortlagde det præcise tidspunkt og geografi for disse ændringer ved hjælp af banebrydende spatial transkriptomik—essensen at skabe et molekylært kort over, hvor og hvornår stress omstrukturerer hjernen. Dette arbejde passer perfekt ind i et voksende billede: psykedelika og relaterede forbindelser som ketamin masker ikke bare symptomer—de ser ud til at afbryde selve den biologiske mekanisme, der driver depression, netop ved dens begyndelse, hvilket åbner døre til at fange og behandle tilstanden meget tidligere end vi kan nu.

items.title: Depression: Ketamine quiets an unruly habenula.

summaries.en: A single dose of ketamine can lift depression within 24 hours—and scientists just discovered why. New research shows that ketamine works by quieting a tiny brain region called the habenula, which normally keeps us stuck in negative thought patterns. When this "worry hub" calms down, our brains stop reinforcing the very things that make us feel bad. Researchers observed this effect in healthy volunteers, tracking how the habenula's activity dropped right when ketamine's antidepressant effects kicked in. This finding matters because it gives us a concrete target: rather than just knowing ketamine works, we're now understanding the actual mechanism, opening doors to develop safer treatments that could help millions without ketamine's risks or legal complications.
summaries.da: En enkelt dosis ketamin kan løfte depression inden for 24 timer—og forskere har lige opdaget hvorfor. Ny forskning viser, at ketamin virker ved at dæmpe en winzig hjernedel kaldet habenula, som normalt holder os fanget i negative tankmønstre. Når dette "bekymringscenter" bliver stille, holder vores hjerner op med at forstærke præcis de ting, der får os til at føle os dårligt. Forskerne observerede denne effekt hos raske frivillige og sporrede, hvordan habenulas aktivitet faldt præcis når ketamins antidepressive virkning satte ind. Dette fund betyder noget, fordi det giver os et konkret mål: i stedet for bare at vide, at ketamin virker, forstår vi nu den faktiske mekanisme, hvilket åbner døre til at udvikle sikrere behandlinger, der kunne hjælpe millioner uden ketamins risici og juridiske komplikationer.

items.title: Ketamine's mechanisms of action in major depressive disorder and treatment-resistant depression: Is brain topological change a candidate convergent systems-level pathway?

summaries.en:
What if depression isn't just a chemical imbalance, but a brain stuck in rigid patterns? New research suggests ketamine works by literally rewiring how different brain regions communicate with each other—and it happens fast, within hours. Instead of just boosting neurotransmitters like traditional antidepressants, ketamine appears to break rigid network patterns and restore flexibility to the brain's communication system, allowing it to reorganize itself in healthier ways.

Scientists reviewed decades of brain imaging and electrical recordings to understand this breakthrough. The findings paint a striking picture: depressed brains show inflexible, disconnected networks, but ketamine rapidly increases connectivity and restores the brain's ability to switch between different states. This systems-level shift—how the whole brain reorganizes rather than isolated molecular changes—may be the real key to why ketamine works so fast for people who haven't responded to anything else. It's reshaping how we think about depression treatment entirely.
summaries.da:
Hvad hvis depression ikke kun handler om kemisk ubalance, men om en hjerne låst fast i stive mønstre? Ny forskning tyder på, at ketamin virker ved at omstille, hvordan forskellige hjernereioner kommunikerer med hinanden—og det sker hurtigt, inden for timer. I stedet for blot at øge signalstoffer som traditionelle antidepressiva, ser ketamin ud til at bryde stive netværksmønstre og genoprette fleksibilitet i hjernens kommunikationssystem, så den kan reorganisere sig selv på sundere måder.

Forskere gennemgik årtiers hjerneafbildning og elektriske målinger for at forstå dette gennembrud. Resultaterne tegner et slående billede: deprimerede hjerner viser ufleksible, afbrudt forbundne netværk, men ketamin øger hurtigt forbindelserne og genopretter hjernens evne til at skifte mellem forskellige tilstande. Denne hele-hjerne-skift—hvordan hele hjernen reorganiserer sig frem for isolerede molekylære ændringer—kan være den rigtige nøgle til, hvorfor ketamin virker så hurtigt for mennesker, der ikke har reageret på andet. Det omformer helt, hvordan vi tænker behandling af depression.

items.title: Psilocybin in Treatment-Resistant Depression: Weighing Rapid Antidepressant Effects Against Uncertain Durability

summaries.en: Imagine taking a single dose of psilocybin and feeling depression lift within weeks—even when nothing else has worked. That's what researchers are seeing in people with treatment-resistant depression, and it's genuinely striking. But here's the honest part: we still don't know how long this relief lasts, or exactly why it works so fast. Scientists reviewed all the latest psilocybin studies (including unpublished phase 3 trials) to figure out what's really happening. The picture emerging is hopeful but complicated—psilocybin paired with psychological support shows real promise, yet the research itself is still messy, with different studies designed so differently that it's hard to compare them. This moment matters because it shows psychedelics could transform how we treat depression, but we need clearer, more rigorous research to turn possibility into practice.
summaries.da: Forestil dig at tage en enkelt dosis psykedelika og mærke depression løfte sig inden for uger—selv når ingenting andet har virket. Det er præcis hvad forskere ser hos mennesker med behandlingsresistent depression, og det er virkeligt slående. Men her er den ærlige del: vi ved stadig ikke hvor længe lettelsen varer, eller præcis hvorfor det virker så hurtigt. Videnskabsfolk gennemgik alle de seneste psykedelika-studier (også uofficielle fase 3-forsøg) for at finde ud af hvad der egentlig sker. Billedet der dukker op er håbefuldt men kompliceret—psykedelika sammen med psykologisk støtte viser reelt potentiale, men forskningen selv er stadig rodet, med så forskellige studiedesign at det er svært at sammenligne dem. Dette øjeblik betyder noget fordi det viser psykedelika kunne transformere hvordan vi behandler depression, men vi skal have klarere, mere grundig forskning for at gøre mulighed til praksis.

items.title: Psychoplastogens to Reduce Persistent Cognitive Symptoms for Traumatic Brain Injury as a Chronic Condition

summaries.en: Millions of people suffer lasting brain fog, memory problems, and cognitive struggles after traumatic brain injury — and right now, there's basically no medication that works. A new review suggests psychedelics like psilocybin and ketamine could be game-changers, because they appear to rewire brain connections in ways that might directly repair the damage TBI causes. Researchers looked at how psychoplastogens (compounds that enhance neuroplasticity) work in the brain and found they target multiple pathways damaged by trauma — from broken neural connections to cellular dysfunction. This emerging research area could finally offer hope to the millions stuck with chronic cognitive symptoms, especially as studies on psychedelics for psychiatric conditions show real promise. The convergence is fascinating: the same brain-repair mechanisms that help depression and PTSD might unlock recovery for people living with TBI's invisible aftermath.
summaries.da: Millioner af mennesker lider af vedvarende hjernetus, hukommelsesproblemer og kognitive vanskeligheder efter traumatisk hjerneskade — og der findes stort set ingen medicin, der virker. Et nyt review foreslår, at psykedelika som psilocybin og ketamin kunne være game-changere, fordi de tilsyneladende kan omvire hjerneforbindelser på måder, der direkte kunne reparere TBI-skaden. Forskere undersøgte, hvordan psykoplastogener (stoffer som forbedrer neuroplasticitet) virker i hjernen, og fandt ud af, at de rammer flere banestier, som traumet beskadiger — fra ødelagte neurale forbindelser til celledysfunktion. Dette nye forskningsområde kunne endelig give håb til de millioner, der lever med kroniske kognitive symptomer fra TBI, især når studier af psykedelika til psykiatriske tilstande viser rigtig resultater. Konvergensen er fascinerende: de samme hjerne-reparationsmekanismer, der hjælper depression og PTSD, kunne låse op for recovery for mennesker, der lever med TBIs usynlige eftervirkninger.

items.title: Biosynthesis of gold nanoparticles using Psilocybe cubensis extracts and their biostimulatory evaluation in Neuro2a cells

summaries.en: Researchers just created tiny gold particles using psilocybin mushrooms—and they might help damaged brain cells recover. When applied to nerve cells in the lab, these nanoparticles sparked cell growth and kept them healthy at the right doses, while the mushroom's natural compounds acted like a protective shield around the gold. Scientists grew gold nanoparticles from Psilocybe cubensis extracts and tested them on neuronal cells, discovering a sweet spot where the particles boosted cell proliferation and viability without harm. This sits at the exciting intersection of green nanotechnology and neuroscience: as psychedelic research expands beyond psychology into biology and medicine, studies like this explore whether psilocybin mushrooms could offer entirely new tools for treating brain injuries and disorders—not just through the psychedelic experience itself, but through the molecules and materials they contain.
summaries.da: Forskere har lige skabt små guldpartikler ved hjælp af psilocybin-svampe—og de kan måske hjælpe skadede hjerneceller til at komme sig. Når guldpartiklerne blev anvendt på nerveceller i laboratoriet, stimulerede de cellevækst og holdt dem raske ved de rigtige doser, mens svampens naturlige stoffer fungerede som et beskyttende skjold omkring guldet. Videnskabsmændene dyrkede guldnanopartikler fra Psilocybe cubensis-ekstrakter og testede dem på nerveceller, hvor de opdagede et ideelt område, hvor partiklerne øgede celleproliferation og levedygtighed uden skade. Dette befinder sig på grænsen mellem grøn nanoteknologi og neurovidenskab: når psykedelika-forskningen ekspanderer ud over psykologi og ind i biologi og medicin, udforsker studier som dette, om psilocybin-svampe kunne tilbyde helt nye værktøjer til behandling af hjerneskader og sygdomme—ikke blot gennem den psykedeliske oplevelse selv, men gennem de molekyler og materialer, de indeholder.

items.title: Investigation of the pharmacological and circuit basis for psychedelic drug effects on interval timing in mice.

summaries.en: Time feels weird on psychedelics — and now we know why. Researchers gave mice psilocin (the active ingredient in magic mushrooms) and found it scrambled their sense of time, making them less accurate at judging short intervals. The cool part? They traced this effect to a specific brain region and serotonin receptor, revealing the actual mechanism behind that trippy time-bending feeling. Using behavioural tests in mice, scientists discovered that blocking one type of serotonin receptor completely stopped the timing distortion, suggesting psychedelics hijack the brain's internal clock through a precise molecular pathway. This fits into a bigger picture: as researchers map out how psychedelics work at the circuit level, we're moving from "they do something to your brain" to understanding exactly what, where, and how — which could eventually help us use these substances more safely and effectively.
summaries.da: Tiden føles underlig på psykedelika — og nu ved vi hvorfor. Forskere gav mus psilocin (det aktive stof i tryllepadder) og fandt ud af, at det forvirrede deres tidsopfattelse og gjorde dem mindre præcise til at bedømme korte tidsintervaller. Det spændende? De sporede denne effekt til en specifik hjernedel og serotoninreceptor, hvilket afslørede den egentlige mekanisme bag den trippy tidsvridning. Ved hjælp af adfærdstests hos mus opdagede forskerne, at blokering af én type serotoninreceptor helt stoppede tidsforvridningen — hvilket tyder på, at psykedelika kaprer hjernens indre ur gennem en præcis molekylær vej. Dette passer ind i et større billede: efterhånden som forskere kortlægger, hvordan psykedelika virker på kredsløbsniveauet, bevæger vi os fra "de gør noget ved din hjerne" til at forstå præcis hvad, hvor og hvordan — hvilket kunne hjælpe os til at bruge disse stoffer mere sikkert og effektivt.

items.title: Buprenorphine Following Ketamine for Suicidal Ideation: A Bridge to Care from the Emergency Department.

summaries.en:
What if a single ketamine session in the emergency room could ease suicidal thoughts enough to let someone actually engage with treatment? New research suggests combining ketamine with buprenorphine might do exactly that — creating a critical window where people in crisis feel stable enough to accept help and stay connected to care. This isn't about a magic cure, but about giving people breathing room when they need it most.

Researchers looked at how ketamine followed by buprenorphine works for people experiencing suicidal ideation in emergency settings. The findings fit into a growing picture: psychedelics and related compounds like ketamine aren't replacing traditional therapy, they're opening doors. They're bridging the gap between crisis and recovery, making it possible for people to actually show up for the longer work ahead.
summaries.da:
Hvad hvis en enkelt ketamin-behandling på skadestuen kunne lette selvmordstanker nok til, at nogen faktisk kunne modtage behandling? Ny forskning tyder på, at kombination af ketamin og buprenorphin gør præcis det — ved at skabe et kritisk tidsvindue, hvor mennesker i krise føler sig stabile nok til at acceptere hjælp og blive ved med at være del af behandlingen. Dette handler ikke om et vidunderkur, men om at give mennesker vejrtrækning, når de har mest brug for det.

Forsker undersøgte, hvordan ketamin fulgt af buprenorphin virker for mennesker med selvmordstanker på skadestuer. Resultaterne passer ind i et voksende billede: psykedelika og beslægtede stoffer som ketamin erstatter ikke traditionel terapi, de åbner døre. De bygger en bro mellem krise og bedring, hvilket gør det muligt for mennesker faktisk at møde op til det længere arbejde, der venter foran.

items.title: Ketamine Extension or Buprenorphine Maintenance?

summaries.en: Ketamine is showing real promise in addiction treatment—but here's the catch: the effects might not last unless you keep using it. A new study compares what happens when you extend ketamine treatment versus switching to buprenorphine maintenance, and the results suggest we need to think differently about how we use these tools together. Researchers tracked patients through both approaches to see which strategy actually keeps people stable long-term. This fits into a bigger shift in psychedelic research: we're moving beyond just asking "does this work?" to the harder questions like "how do we use it wisely?" and "what comes after?" Ketamine's rapid anti-craving effects could be revolutionary for addiction, but the real breakthrough might be combining it with other treatments—something that could reshape how we think about recovery.
summaries.da: Ketamin viser sig lovende i behandlingen af afhængighed—men her er sagen: effekterne holder måske ikke uden du fortsætter med at bruge det. Et nyt studie sammenligner hvad der sker når man forlænger ketaminbehandlingen versus skifter til buprenorfin-vedligeholdelse, og resultaterne tyder på at vi skal tænke anderledes om hvordan vi bruger disse værktøjer sammen. Forskere fulgte patienter gennem begge tilgange for at se hvilken strategi der rent faktisk holder mennesker stabile på længere sigt. Dette passer ind i et større skift inden for psykedelika-forskningen: vi bevæger os væk fra bare at spørge "virker det?" til de sværere spørgsmål som "hvordan bruger vi det klogt?" og "hvad kommer efter?" Ketamins hurtige anti-craving-effekter kunne være revolutionerende for afhængighed, men det rigtige gennembrud handler måske om at kombinere det med anden behandling—noget der kunne ændre hvordan vi tænker omkring recovery.

items.title: Buprenorphine After Ketamine for Suicidal Ideation: Durability, Specificity, and Confounding.

summaries.en: Ketamine has shown remarkable promise for people struggling with suicidal thoughts — offering rapid relief where traditional antidepressants often fall short. But a crucial question has lingered: how long does this effect actually last, and what happens next? A new study digs into this by examining what occurs when buprenorphine (an opioid medication) is given after ketamine treatment, exploring whether the benefits hold steady and what's really driving the improvement. This matters because understanding the durability and specifics of ketamine's effects is essential as researchers work toward making it a reliable part of suicide prevention. As psychedelics and novel compounds like ketamine move from fringe experiments into serious clinical consideration, studies like this help build the careful, detailed evidence base needed to transform how we treat mental health crises.
summaries.da: Ketamin har vist bemærkelsesværdig potentiale for mennesker, der kæmper med selvmordstanker — det giver hurtig lindring, hvor traditionelle antidepressiver ofte svigter. Men ét afgørende spørgsmål har været ubesvaret: hvor længe varer virkningen egentlig, og hvad sker der derefter? Et nyt studie udforsker dette ved at undersøge, hvad der sker, når buprenorfin (et opioid) gives efter ketaminbehandling, og hvad der reelt driver forbedringen. Det er vigtig viden, fordi vi skal forstå ketamins varige effekt for at gøre det til en pålidelig del af selvmordsforebyggelse. Mens psykedelika og nye stoffer som ketamin bevæger sig fra marginale eksperimenter mod seriøs klinisk praksis, hjælper studier som dette med at bygge det grundige bevisgrundlag, som er nødvendigt for at transformere, hvordan vi behandler mental sundhedskriser.

items.title: Low-Dose Buprenorphine Significantly Prolonging the Antisuicidal Effects of Ketamine Infusion in Major Depressive Disorder: Relationship Between Antidepressant and Antisuicidal Effects.

summaries.en: What if a simple add-on could make ketamine's life-saving effects last way longer? New research suggests that combining low-dose buprenorphine with ketamine infusions dramatically extends how long people stay protected from suicidal thoughts—and it's not just because the depression lifts. Scientists gave some depressed patients ketamine alone, others with buprenorphine added to the mix, and tracked their suicidal urges over time. The results hint at something fascinating: buprenorphine seems to protect the brain's anti-suicide benefits even as other symptoms improve at different rates. This fits perfectly into where ketamine research is heading—moving beyond just "does it work?" toward "how do we make it work better and longer?" As ketamine clinics pop up around the world, finding ways to extend its protective window could be genuinely life-changing for people in crisis.
summaries.da: Hvad hvis en simpel tilføjelse kunne få ketamins livsvigtige effekter til at vare meget længere? Ny forskning tyder på, at når man kombinerer lavdosis buprenorphin med ketamininfusioner, forlænges det betydeligt, hvor længe mennesker er beskyttet mod selvmordstanker—og det skyldes ikke bare, at depressionen forsvinder. Forskerne gav nogle deprimerede patienter ketamin alene, andre med buprenorphin tilføjet, og fulgte deres selvmordsuges over tid. Resultaterne peger på noget fascinerende: buprenorphin virker til at beskytte hjernens anti-selvmord-fordele selv når andre symptomer bedres i forskelligt tempo. Det passer perfekt ind i, hvor ketaminforskningen er på vej hen—væk fra bare "virker det?" hen imod "hvordan får vi det til at virke bedre og længere?" Mens ketaminklinikker dukker op verden over, kunne det at finde måder til at forlænge dets beskyttelsesvindue være virkelig livreddende for mennesker i krise.

items.title: Ketamine in psychiatry: a systematic review of clinical applications, safety considerations, and emerging challenges.

summaries.en: Ketamine is having a quiet revolution in psychiatry. Once used only as an anesthetic, it's now showing remarkable promise for treatment-resistant depression and chronic pain—often working within hours rather than weeks. What makes it special? It works differently than traditional antidepressants, triggering rapid changes in brain chemistry that literally rebuild neural connections. Researchers conducted a systematic review of 106 peer-reviewed studies to understand how ketamine actually works in the brain and where it's being used clinically. This fits into a broader shift happening right now: psychiatry is moving beyond older medications toward faster-acting, mechanism-based treatments. Ketamine's success is opening doors for how we think about mental health—but it also raises real questions about safety, recreational use, and access that the field is grappling with head-on.
summaries.da: Ketamin gennemgår en stille revolution inden for psykiatrien. Det blev engang kun brugt som narkosemiddel, men viser nu bemærkelsesværdigt potentiale til behandling af depressioner, der ikke reagerer på andre medicin, og kroniske smerter—ofte med effekt inden for timer snarere end uger. Hvad gør det særligt? Det virker anderledes end traditionelle antidepressiva og udløser hurtige ændringer i hjernekemien, der bogstaveligt talt genopbygger nerveforbindelser. Forskere gennemgik systematisk 106 peer-reviewed studier for at forstå, hvordan ketamin virker i hjernen og hvor det bruges klinisk. Dette passer ind i en større skift, der sker lige nu: psykiatrien bevæger sig væk fra ældre medicin mod hurtigere virkende, mekanisme-baserede behandlinger. Ketamins succes åbner døre for, hvordan vi tænker om mental sundhed—men det rejser også reelle spørgsmål om sikkerhed, rekreativt misbrug og adgang, som området aktivt arbejder med.

items.title: Serotonin 1B receptors expressed on forebrain excitatory neurons mediate the post-acute anxiolytic response to psilocybin in mice

summaries.en:
Scientists just figured out how psilocybin helps ease anxiety—and it's surprisingly specific. A new study in mice reveals that psilocybin's anxiety-busting effects don't happen during the trip itself, but *after*, through a particular type of serotonin receptor in the brain's excitatory neurons. This matters because it means the calming benefits might stick around even after the acute effects wear off—a genuine shift from trip to lasting relief.

Researchers used genetic techniques to pinpoint exactly which brain cells and receptors were responsible, narrowing down a process that's been a mystery for years. This kind of precise mechanistic work is exactly what's pushing psychedelic science forward right now: moving beyond "does it work?" to "how does it work, specifically?" Understanding these neural pathways opens doors for developing better treatments and potentially creating compounds that capture the therapeutic benefits without requiring a full psychedelic experience.
summaries.da:
Videnskabsmænd har lige løst et puslespil omkring psykedelika og angst—og svaret er bemærkelsesværdigt præcist. Et nyt studie hos mus viser, at psykedelikas angstdæmpende effekter ikke sker under trippen selv, men *efter*, gennem en særlig type serotoninreceptor i hjernens excitatoriske neuroner. Det betyder, at den beroligende virkning kunne blive siddende længe efter, at det akutte forløber—et rigtigt skift fra trip til vedvarende lettelse.

Forskerne brugte genetiske teknikker til at pege nøjagtigt på, hvilke hjerneceller og receptorer der var ansvarlige, og løste dermed et mysterium, der har været uafklaret i årevis. Det her præcise arbejde er præcist det, der driver psykedelisk forskning fremad lige nu: at gå fra "virker det?" til "hvordan virker det præcist?" Når vi forstår disse neurale veje, åbner det døre for bedre behandlinger og potentielt stofforme, der fanger terapieffekterne uden at kræve en fuldstændig psykedelisk oplevelse.

items.title: Ketamine administration reduced conditioned defensive behaviour and upregulated protein expression associated with neuroplasticity in a planarian model of aversive memory reactivation.

summaries.en: Traumatic memories can feel stuck, replaying over and over in people with PTSD. A new study shows ketamine might help unstick them—when memories are reactivated, ketamine seems to soften their grip, making them feel less threatening. Researchers used a simple organism called planaria to understand how: ketamine didn't erase the memory, but triggered the brain's natural ability to update and rewire it, boosting the proteins involved in neuroplasticity. This builds on growing evidence that ketamine works best when combined with memory reactivation, opening a genuinely new path for treating trauma—not by forgetting, but by helping the brain reprocess what happened.
summaries.da: Traumatiske minder kan føles fastlåst, de gentager sig igen og igen for mennesker med PTSD. En ny undersøgelse viser, at psykedelika som ketamin kunne hjælpe med at løsne dem—når minder reaktiveres, ser ketamin ud til at mildne deres greb, så de føles mindre truende. Forskere brugte en simpel organisme kaldet planaria til at forstå hvordan: ketamin slettede ikke mindet, men udløste hjernens naturlige evne til at opdatere og omkablere det, og styrkede de proteiner, der er involveret i neuroplasticitet. Dette bygger på voksende evidens for, at ketamin virker bedst når det kombineres med mindeaktivering, og åbner en genuint ny vej for behandling af traumer—ikke ved at glemme, men ved at hjælpe hjernen med at genbearbejde det, der skete.

items.title: What goes up must comedown: prevalence rates, characteristics, and coping strategies concerning MDMA aftereffects.

summaries.en: Three out of four MDMA users experience a rough comedown—and scientists just mapped exactly what that looks like. A new study of nearly 500 people found that most experience fatigue, brain fog, and restlessness starting about a day after use, typically lasting around 40 hours. The findings are sobering: some users report serious mood crashes, including suicidal thoughts. Researchers surveyed people about their real-world experiences and what actually helps them cope, from supplements to other strategies. As psychedelics move closer to becoming mainstream medicine, understanding what happens after the trip ends matters enormously—not just for recreational users, but for therapists and patients considering these compounds as treatments. This research fills a gap: we've focused heavily on psychedelics' potential benefits, but managing the harder days afterward is just as crucial to getting this right.
summaries.da: Tre ud af fire personer, der bruger MDMA, oplever et hårdt nedtur—og nu har forskerne kortlagt præcist, hvad det ser ud til. Et nyt studie med næsten 500 personer viser, at de fleste oplever træthed, mentalt tåget og rastløshed omkring en dag efter brug, typisk varende omkring 40 timer. Resultaterne er alvorlige: nogle brugere rapporterer dybe humørfalд, herunder selvmordstanker. Forskerne spurgte mennesker om deres virkelige erfaringer og hvad der faktisk hjælper dem, fra kosttilskud til andre strategier. I takt med at psykedelika nærmer sig mainstream-medicin, betyder det enormt meget at forstå, hvad der sker efter tripet ender—ikke blot for rekreative brugere, men for terapeuter og patienter, der overvejer disse stoffer som behandlinger. Denne forskning udfylder et tomrum: vi har fokuseret stærkt på psykedelikas potentielle fordele, men at håndtere de sværere dage efter er lige så vigtig for at få det rigtigt.

items.title: Beyond psychedelic exceptionalism: how people combine meditation with psychoactive substances, and how this relates to well-being

summaries.en:
Most people combining meditation with substances aren't using classic psychedelics at all—they're meditating with alcohol, cannabis, and nicotine. A new study of nearly 1,400 people flips the script on what we thought we knew: only 6% paired meditation with classic psychedelics, while 29% combined it with alcohol. The research suggests that mixing mind-body practices with substances might be more mainstream than the psychedelic-focused narrative lets on.

In a detailed follow-up with 397 participants, researchers found something intriguing: people using harder drugs without meditation showed worse well-being outcomes, but those same people doing both showed no such decline. It's early evidence suggesting meditation might matter more than the substance itself. As psychedelic science matures beyond focusing solely on classic compounds, this work points to a bigger question: how do different practices and substances interact with our mental health in real life?
summaries.da:
De fleste mennesker, der kombinerer meditation med stoffer, bruger slet ikke klassiske psykedelika—de mediterer med alkohol, cannabis og nikotin. Et nyt studie af næsten 1.400 personer vendt op og ned på, hvad vi troede vi vidste: kun 6% kombinerede meditation med klassiske psykedelika, mens 29% gjorde det med alkohol. Forskningen tyder på, at blanding af mind-body-praksis med stoffer er mere almindelig, end psykedelika-fokuseret fortælling får det til at virke.

I en detaljeret opfølgning med 397 deltagere opdagede forskerne noget fascinerende: mennesker, der brugte hårdere stoffer uden meditation, viste dårligere velbefindende, men de samme mennesker, der gjorde begge dele, viste ingen sådan nedgang. Det er tidlig evidens for, at meditation måske betyder mere end stoffet selv. Efterhånden som psykedelika-forskningen udvikler sig ud over klassiske forbindelser, peger dette arbejde på et større spørgsmål: hvordan interagerer forskellige praksisser og stoffer med vores mentale sundhed i virkeligheden?

items.title: French psychiatric caregivers' perceptions of psychedelics: A national survey.

summaries.en: French psychiatrists and psychologists are warming up to psychedelics—but with caution. A new survey of nearly 300 mental health professionals found that 53% see real therapeutic promise in substances like psilocybin and LSD, especially for treatment-resistant depression. Yet most remain skeptical about recreational use, and many know surprisingly little about psychedelics beyond the headlines. Researchers asked French caregivers about their knowledge and attitudes toward psychedelics in a December 2023–January 2024 survey, just as France was launching its first official clinical trials. The findings matter because they show where the psychiatric establishment stands as psychedelic research accelerates globally—and what gaps need filling. Right now, openness to psychedelics among French mental health professionals sits somewhere between curiosity and caution, a realistic snapshot of how mainstream medicine is slowly, thoughtfully reconsidering these compounds.
summaries.da: Franske psykiatere og psykologer bliver mere åbne over for psykedelika—men med forsigtighed. En ny undersøgelse af knap 300 psykiske sundhedsprofessionelle viser, at 53% ser reel terapeutisk potentiale i stoffer som psilocybin og LSD, især til behandlingsresistent depression. Alligevel er de fleste skeptiske over for rekreativt brug, og mange ved overraskende lidt om psykedelika ud over mediebråk. Forskere spurgte franske sundhedspersonale om deres viden og holdninger til psykedelika i december 2023–januar 2024, lige da Frankrig lancerede sine første officielle kliniske forsøg. Resultaterne betyder noget, fordi de viser hvor det psykiatriske establishment står, mens psykedelika-forskningen accelererer globalt—og hvor der er huller at fylde. Lige nu ligger åbenhedet blandt franske psykiske sundhedsprofessionelle et sted mellem nysgerrighed og forsigtighed, et realistisk billede af, hvordan medicinen langsomt, tankefuldt overvejer disse stoffer på ny.

items.title: After the Trip: A Qualitative Study of Healthy Individuals' Motor Experiences Following Different Doses of Psilocybin.

summaries.en: Your body feels different on psychedelics—but maybe not in the way you'd think. New research found that people on psilocybin report surprisingly mixed experiences with movement: some feel clumsy or slow, others feel more fluid and connected to their bodies. Interestingly, these motor shifts seem dose-dependent, meaning the strength of the experience really matters. Researchers interviewed 12 healthy participants about their physical sensations after doing movement tasks on different amounts of psilocybin, then carefully analyzed what they said. This work fills a real gap in psychedelic science—we know a lot about the mind-bending aspects, but less about how your nervous system actually experiences its own movement. As researchers push toward therapeutic uses, understanding these physical dimensions matters for safety and helping people have better experiences.
summaries.da: Din krop føles anderledes på psykedelika—men måske ikke som du skulle tro. Ny forskning viser, at mennesker på psilocybin rapporterer overraskende blandede oplevelser med bevægelse: nogle føler sig klumset eller langsomme, andre føler sig mere flydende og forbundne med deres kroppe. Interessant nok synes disse motoriske skift at være dosisafhængige, hvilket betyder, at styrken af oplevelsen virkelig betyder noget. Forskerne interviewede 12 raske deltagere om deres fysiske fornemmelser efter at have udført bevægelsesopgaver ved forskellige mængder psilocybin og analyserede derefter omhyggeligt det, de sagde. Dette arbejde udfylder et reelt hul i psykedelika-forskningen—vi ved meget om de sindsbevægende aspekter, men mindre om, hvordan dit nervesystem faktisk oplever sin egen bevægelse. Når forskere arbejder mod terapeutiske anvendelser, betyder det at forstå disse fysiske dimensioner noget for sikkerhed og for at hjælpe mennesker med at få bedre oplevelser.

items.title: Coding and Classification Errors in Study of Psilocybin Services

summaries.en: A new study has caught some important mistakes in how psilocybin services are being tracked and classified — and that matters more than you'd think. When researchers looked at the data, they found coding errors that could make it harder to actually understand what's working in these emerging treatment programmes. Getting the details right isn't boring bureaucracy; it's the foundation for knowing whether psilocybin therapy really helps people and how to do it better. The researchers reviewed existing datasets to spot these problems, shining a light on a gap in how we're documenting this rapidly growing field. As psilocybin services expand globally and research accelerates, having clear, consistent standards matters hugely — it's the difference between hype and solid science.
summaries.da: En ny undersøgelse har afsløret vigtige fejl i, hvordan psilocybin-tjenester bliver registreret og klassificeret — og det betyder mere end du tror. Da forskere kiggede på dataene, fandt de kodningsfejl, der kunne gøre det sværere at forstå, hvad der virker i disse nye behandlingsprogrammer. At få detaljerne rigtigt er ikke kedeligt bureaukrati; det er grundlaget for at vide, om psilocybin-terapi virkelig hjælper mennesker og hvordan vi gør det bedre. Forskerne gennemgik eksisterende datasæt for at finde disse problemer og kastede lys på et hul i, hvordan vi dokumenterer dette hurtigt voksende felt. Efterhånden som psilocybin-tjenester ekspanderer globalt og forskningen accelererer, betyder klare, ensartede standarder enormt meget — det er forskellen mellem hype og solid videnskab.

items.title: Adverse outcomes of psychedelics self‐reported: Survey

summaries.en:
A major U.S. survey reveals which psychedelics cause the most problems: ibogaine and 5-MeO-DMT topped the list for adverse effects per dose, while psilocybin, LSD, and MDMA caused more total problems simply because more people use them. Ibogaine stood out for heart risks, which researchers already knew to watch for. This matters because these substances are now in serious clinical trials for depression, anxiety, and other psychiatric conditions—and we need honest data about what can go wrong to help doctors and patients make informed decisions.

The researchers surveyed nearly 2,000 American adults about their experiences over the past year, making this one of the first large-scale snapshots of real-world safety. While the study can't prove cause-and-effect, it adds crucial ground-truth to the conversation happening in labs and clinics right now: psychedelics show genuine promise, but they're not risk-free, and different substances carry different dangers.
summaries.da:
En stor amerikansk undersøgelse afslører, hvilke psykedelika der forårsager flest problemer: ibogain og 5-MeO-DMT toppede listen for bivirkninger pr. dosis, mens psilocybin, LSD og MDMA forårsagede flere samlede problemer, simpelthen fordi flere mennesker bruger dem. Ibogain skiller sig ud for hjertekomplikationer, som forskere allerede vidste, man skulle være opmærksom på. Det betyder noget, fordi disse stoffer nu er i seriøse kliniske forsøg for depression, angst og andre psykiatriske tilstande—og vi har brug for ærlig data om, hvad der kan gå galt, så læger og patienter kan træffe informerede beslutninger.

Forskerne adspurgte næsten 2.000 amerikanske voksne om deres erfaringer over det seneste år, hvilket gør dette til et af de første store øjebliksbilleder af sikkerhed i den virkelige verden. Selvom studiet ikke kan bevise årsag og virkning, tilføjer det vigtig indsigt til samtalen, der foregår på laboratorier og klinikker lige nu: psykedelika viser ægte løfte, men de er ikke risikofrie, og forskellige stoffer bærer forskellige farer.

items.title: Ultra-High-Performance Liquid Chromatography-High Resolution Mass Spectrometry and Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry Screening of Classical Psychoactive Substances, Novel Psychoactive Substances, and Metabolites in Postmortem Urine Samples

summaries.en:
Researchers have developed a sophisticated new way to detect psychedelics and their metabolites in postmortem samples—a breakthrough that could transform how forensic scientists understand deaths involving these substances. Using advanced chemical analysis techniques, scientists can now identify not just what someone took, but also trace the byproducts their body created, painting a much clearer picture than ever before.

This Danish study represents a crucial shift in how we approach psychedelic research scientifically. By creating better forensic tools, researchers aren't just solving mysteries—they're building the foundation for understanding how these substances interact with human biology at the deepest level. As psychedelics move from underground into clinical trials and legitimate research, having this kind of precise analytical capability matters enormously for safety, regulation, and our growing knowledge of how these compounds actually work.
summaries.da:
Forskere har udviklet en sofistikeret ny metode til at opdage psykedelika og deres metabolitter i obduktionsprøver—et gennembrud, der kunne transformere, hvordan retsmedicinere forstår dødsfald involverende disse stoffer. Ved hjælp af avancerede kemiske analyseteknikker kan videnskabsmændene nu identificere ikke bare hvad nogen tog, men også spore de biprodukter deres krop dannede, hvilket giver et meget klarere billede end nogensinde før.

Denne danske undersøgelse repræsenterer et afgørende skift i, hvordan vi behandler psykedelika-forskning videnskabeligt. Ved at skabe bedre retsmedicinske værktøjer bygger forskerne ikke bare på løsning af mysterier—de konstruerer fundamentet for at forstå, hvordan disse stoffer interagerer med menneskelig biologi på det dybeste niveau. Efterhånden som psykedelika bevæger sig fra underjorden ind i kliniske forsøg og legitim forskning, betyder denne præcise analytiske kapacitet enormt meget for sikkerhed, regulering og vores voksende kendskab til, hvordan disse forbindelser faktisk virker.

items.title: Aspirational Autonomy and Psychedelic-Assisted Therapy in Advanced Cancer: Ethical Lessons from Clinical Cases.

summaries.en: What if the point of psychedelics for dying patients isn't just feeling better—but becoming who you want to be in your final chapter? New research on psilocybin-assisted therapy in advanced cancer shows that when it works, it's often because people find new clarity, courage, or peace with themselves and their lives. Not mystical experiences or symptom checklists, but real shifts in how patients relate to themselves and others. Researchers studied three patient cases from a clinical trial and found something important: meaningful consent for this kind of therapy doesn't require predicting the unpredictable. Instead, it's about patients choosing to embark on a supported journey of existential exploration. The work reveals practical challenges oncologists need to navigate—managing expectations, embracing uncertainty, and supporting integration when time is short. As psychedelics move closer to clinical reality for people facing end-of-life anxiety and distress, this research offers crucial guidance on who might benefit most and how to do this ethically.
summaries.da: Hvad hvis pointen med psykedelika for døende patienter ikke bare er at føle sig bedre—men at blive den person, man gerne vil være i sin afsluttende tid? Ny forskning på psilocybin-assisteret terapi ved fremskreden kræft viser, at når det virker, skyldes det ofte, at mennesker finder ny klarhed, mod eller fred med sig selv og deres liv. Ikke mystiske oplevelser eller symptomreduktion, men ægte skift i, hvordan patienter forholder sig til sig selv og andre. Forskere studerede tre patienttilfælde fra et klinisk forsøg og fandt noget vigtigt: meningsfuld samtykke til denne type terapi kræver ikke, at man forudsiger det uforudsigelige. I stedet handler det om, at patienter vælger at begive sig på en understøttet rejse af eksistentiel udforskning. Arbejdet afslørede praktiske udfordringer, som onkologer skal navigere—håndtere forventninger, omfavne usikkerhed og støtte integration når tiden er knap. Efterhånden som psykedelika nærmer sig klinisk virkelighed for mennesker, der står over for angst og eksistentiel lidelse ved livets afslutning, giver denne forskning vigtig vejledning om, hvem der kunne have gavn heraf og hvordan man gør det etisk.

items.title: Ketamine and Esketamine in Acute Suicidal Presentations: Evidence, Limits, and a Conceptual Recovery-Enabling Downstaging Framework.

summaries.en:
Ketamine and esketamine show promise for rapidly easing suicidal thoughts in people in crisis—sometimes within hours rather than days. But here's what matters: these aren't magic bullets. The research shows they can calm the immediate storm, yet we don't yet have solid proof they prevent actual suicide attempts or deaths. In recent clinical trials, esketamine worked best when paired with hospitalization, new antidepressants, and full supportive care—suggesting it's a powerful first step, not a standalone solution.

Scientists reviewed decades of evidence to understand exactly what these ketamine treatments do and don't do. What's emerging is a clearer picture: psychedelics and related compounds like ketamine fit into emergency suicide care as part of a bigger toolkit. The real breakthrough isn't just the rapid relief—it's recognizing that getting someone through the crisis moment is only the beginning. The future of mental health emergency care means combining these fast-acting interventions with solid aftercare, proper medication, and genuine support. That's where the real transformation happens.
summaries.da:
Ketamin og esketamin viser lovende resultater til at lindre selvmordstanker hos mennesker i krise—nogle gange inden for timer i stedet for dage. Men her er det vigtige: de er ikke tryllekuler. Forskningen viser, at de kan dæmpe den umiddelbare storm, men vi har endnu ikke solid bevis for, at de forhindrer faktiske selvmordsforsøg eller dødsfald. I nylige kliniske forsøg fungerede esketamin bedst kombineret med hospitalsindlæggelse, nye antidepressiva og fuld støttende behandling—hvilket tyder på, at det er et kraftfuldt første skridt, ikke en selvstændig løsning.

Forskere gennemgik årtiers bevis for at forstå præcis, hvad disse ketaminbehandlinger gør og ikke gør. Det, der opstår, er et klarere billede: psykedelika og lignende stoffer som ketamin passer ind i akut selvmordsbehandling som en del af en større værktøjskasse. Det virkelige gennembrud er ikke blot den hurtige lindring—det er at erkende, at det at få nogen gennem krisetidspunktet kun er begyndelsen. Fremtiden for psykisk sundhedsbehandling betyder at kombinere disse hurtigt virkende interventioner med solid efterbehandling, passende medicin og ægte støtte. Det er hvor den virkelige transformation sker.
